entry.title: The Gravity of the Default Path: When the “Interface” Makes Choices for Us
entry.summary: In 1956, the U.S. Congress wrote down a number: 90%. The federal government would cover 90%, and state governments 10%, to build the Interstate Highway System. Sixty years later, that single ratio shaped where hundreds of millions of Americans live, how they commute, and whether they can afford a home. No one voted for suburban sprawl. Yet almost no one could refuse it. This is not fate. This is an interface. If you understand 90/10 as merely a “fiscal subsidy ratio,” you miss its most important structural force.
